question: A cryogenic engine makes use of which of the following as its fuel?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liquid Oxygen and liquid hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A cryogenic engine is a type of rocket engine that utilizes cryogenic propellants which are liquids.
 
• **Liquid Hydrogen (LH2):** Typically used as the** fuel.**
 
• **Liquid Oxygen (LOX):** Commonly used as the **oxidizer**
 
• These propellants are stored at temperatures below their boiling points:** −253°C (−423°F) **for liquid hydrogen and** −183°C (−297°F) **for liquid oxygen

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Different types of engines in rockets are**

 
• **Solid Rocket Engines** -Use** solid propellants**, which are a mixture of fuel and oxidizer bound together.
 
• **Liquid Rocket Engines** -There are two main types of liquid rocket engines:** bipropellant and monopropellant**
 
• **Hybrid Rocket Engines** -Combine elements of** both solid and liquid** engines. Typically, use a **solid fuel** and a **liquid or** **gaseous oxidizer**
 
• **Electric Propulsion Engines** -Electric propulsion uses** electrical energy** to accelerate propellant ions.
 
• **Nuclear Thermal and Nuclear Electric Engines (Experimental/Advanced)** -Uses a nuclear reactor to heat a propellant like **hydrogen**.
